case.summary: Customer C11923 reported an unauthorized $131.30 online transaction (3583368) on 2016-12-29. The transaction was made from a device marked as new to the account (SM-G610F Build/NRD90M, chrome 66.0 for android) and the amount is more than four times the cardholder's median transaction value of $28.55 across 10361 historical transactions. The card_not_present_new_device pattern matched at 0.57 strength, consistent with similar closed cases retrieved from account history: all 8 structurally similar prior cases were confirmed fraud. The account itself carries 10 prior confirmed-fraud cases, including 4 with matching patterns. Exposure for this episode totals $3984.80 across 84 transactions. Given the customer's explicit denial, the anomalous transaction amount relative to baseline spending, the new device usage, and the strong historical precedent on this account and pattern, I conclude this transaction is fraud with high confidence of 0.77.

sar.narrative: Customer C11923 reported an unauthorized $131.30 online purchase on card C11923-K2 made on 2016-12-29 at 03:27:44. The transaction was processed through an online channel for product code C. The transaction was executed using a device profile (SM-G610F Build/NRD90M, chrome 66.0 for android) that the bank's records mark as new to this account. The activity is suspicious for several reasons. The transaction amount of $131.30 is more than four times the cardholder's median transaction size of $28.55 across 10,361 transactions over a five-month period ending 2016-12-29. The device used was new to the account and is shared with another account (C08962), which presents elevated risk for card-not-present fraud. The cardholder has a history of confirmed fraud cases including at least four prior instances flagged for card-not-present-new-device and card-testing patterns. Six structurally similar closed cases involving the same device-sharing and pattern characteristics were all confirmed as fraud, indicating this device and pattern combination has a strong history of fraudulent use on this account. Beyond the flagged transaction, an 84-transaction episode beginning 2016-12-27 at 03:33:30 shows rapid-fire purchases of similar amounts (primarily in the $92-93 range) occurring in the early morning hours, consistent with automated or scripted card testing activity. The total suspicious exposure identified in this episode is $3,984.80. The bank created a case, is monitoring connected cards, and is blocking card C11923-K2. A report will be filed with the financial regulator.
